Text: Equalise utility charges and other costs between rural and urban areas.  Develop a comprehensive programme to address the needs of our islands.  Acting while there is still time.  Fianna Fáil believe that the time has now come to create a radical new programme aimed at restoring the balance of our population between urban and rural areas.  If we do not act now, many rural communities will lose their viability and the depopulation trend will become irreversible. Meanwhile, the overbalanced growth of our large urban areas is creating social problems we can no longer ignore. Stimulating rural development will take some of the increasing pressure off our cities. Fianna Fáil’s rural development policy is based on recognising a number of basic realities.  - First, people will always go where the jobs are. Without adequate employment in rural areas, depopulation is inevitable.  - Second, agriculture can no longer on its own hope to sustain rural communities. Fianna Fáil’s policy is to keep as many farm families as possible on the land, but other forms of activity must exist to supplement the core contribution that agriculture makes. Increasingly, we see future job creation in rural areas in the services sector.  - Third, rural development cannot succeed fully until people in rural areas can get the same range and quality of services as in urban areas and at the same price. Too often, people living and working in rural areas do so under a handicap.  - Fourth, new technology particularly in communications now offers for the first time an opportunity to provide economically a wide range of services at truly local level. Technology now also makes it possible to run many more types of business from a rural base.  Eleven steps on the road to population stability.  Fianna Fáil in government will  1. Begin an energetic programme of localisation of state services that are now provided centrally. 

Summary:
chosen:
- Equalise utility charges and develop a comprehensive rural programme to restore population balance between urban and rural areas.  
- Rural depopulation threatens community viability unless jobs are created; agriculture alone cannot suffice, and services sector growth is key.  
- Rural residents must receive the same range, quality, and price of services as urban residents.  
- New communication technologies enable economically viable, locally delivered services and allow many businesses to operate from rural locations.  
- The policy will start by localising state services currently delivered centrally.

Text: The reason is that the new age offers us, for the first time since the Industrial Revolution, a way around the disadvantages we have always suffered because of our remote position on the periphery of Europe. In the Information Age, where we are will no longer matter. Ireland will be as well-placed as any country in a truly global market-place, if we have the right infrastructure in place. Indeed, because of the calibre of our people, Ireland is ideally positioned to become a leader in a world that will be dominated by knowledge industries. However, this opportunity must be grasped, the dividend from the Information Age will not come to us automatically. On the contrary: if we do not prepare properly, we will be left behind. If we fail to meet the challenge, the information age could undermine much of the economic success we have enjoyed so far. We must ready ourselves for the new era in two main ways. First, through the education system, preparing our people for a totally new way of doing things. Second, through our communications infrastructure, making sure that our people have full, low-cost access to the tools that make the new ways possible. In both these critical sectors, we are already behind. In both these areas the Rainbow Government has failed the people of Ireland. A recent survey showed Ireland to be, not in the vanguard of information age readiness where we could and should be, but in the third division of countries.  Educating for a new age.  In Fianna Fáil’s education Green Paper of 1992, we clearly signalled the coming significance of information technology in education. Fianna Fáil’s policy document on Information Technology in Education, published earlier this year, led the way in proposing a radical new departure. Since then the Rainbow Government has issued its own 5-year programme. Where appropriate or worthwhile, Fianna Fáil will incorporate elements of that programme into our own much more wide-ranging policy. 

Summary:
chosen: The passage argues that Ireland’s remote European position no longer limits its prospects in the Information Age, provided it invests in education and low‑cost communications infrastructure. It contends that these two sectors are essential for turning the new age into an opportunity and accuses the Rainbow Government of failing to act, leaving Ireland behind in global market readiness. The text cites a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT policy proposals as models for the needed reforms, warning that without proper preparation Ireland risks losing the economic benefits of the Information Age.

Text: Er teilte dem Parteirat mit, daß eine Finanzierungskommission gebildet Wurde, der Sozialisten angehören, die durch ihre Funktion im öffentlichen Leben und durch ihre Leistungen bewiesen haben, daß sie mit Geld umgehen können und die ihnen überantworteten Mittel gut verwalten. Diese Männer haben die sozialistischen Programme geprüft und in einem Gutachten als finanzierbar erklärt.  Der Kommission gehörten an: Die Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Doktor Schachner,  Suchanek und Dr. Vogl und die Bürgermeister von Landeshauptstädten Marek, Dipl.Ing. Scherbaum, Hillinger und Bäck. Diese Männer, betonte Kreisky, verwalten öffentliche Mittel von nahezu 30 Milliarden Schilling. Zusätzlich prüften und unterzeichneten das Gutachten noch der Generaldirektorstellvertreter der Nationalbank Dr. Kienzl sowie Dr. Veselsky und Direktor Dr. Uher (Länderbank).  Grundlage für die Politik der siebziger Jahre  Kreisky beschäftigte sich dann im einzelnen mit der Alternative der Sozialisten. Sie umfaßt Leitlinien der Außenpolitik, das Humanprogramm, das Kultur und Bildungsprogramm, das Wirtschaftsprogramm mit dem Verkehrskonzept und die Programme zur Verbesserung der staatlichen Einrichtungen Parlament, Justiz, Verwaltung und Bundesheer. Diese Programme bilden die Grundlage der Politik der Sozialistischen Partei für die siebziger Jahre.  Neuer Start für EFTAEWG  Zur Integrationspolitik sagte er, daß nun, da auch Frankreich sich vom altmodischen Gleichgewichtsdenken zu lösen beginnt, ein Fortschritt in der europäischen Integration erreicht werden könnte. Dabei sei zu berücksichtigen, daß es nicht nur die EWG und EFTA gibt, sondern innerhalb der EFTAStaaten, die den Beitritt zur EWG wollen und solche, die ein Nahverhältnis wünschen. Das Klügste wäre wohl, wenn sich die EWG und die EFTAStaaten einmal grundsätzlich zur wirtschaftlichen Zusammenarbeit bereit erklärten. Von hier weg sollten dann Lösungen für einen Ausgleich zwischen den beiden Wirtschaftsgemeinschaften gesucht werden.  

Summary:
chosen: A financing commission, composed of socialist officials (Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck) and auditors (Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher), was formed to audit and certify socialist programmes as financially viable, managing nearly 30 billion Schilling in public funds. These programmes cover foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative and military institutions, forming the basis of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda. Kreisky argues that, as France moves beyond traditional balance thinking, cooperation between the EWG and EFTA should be pursued, aiming to balance the economies of the two blocs.

Text:  Der Parteivorsitzende legte dann die Grundzüge der einzelnen Programme dar. Das Wirtschaftsprogramm sei heute wichtiger denn je, weil die ÖVP aus einem Propagandabedürfnis heraus eine Prosperitätseuphorie betreibe etwas, vor dem in anderen Ländern immer gewarnt werde. Di Hochkonjunktur überdecke falsche Wirtschaftsstrukturen jedoch nur zeitweise.  Für permanente Demokratisierung  Die Sozialdemokraten, setzte Kreisky fort, sind froh darüber, daß die Diskussion über die Demokratie nun überall in Gang gekommen ist, ist es doch ihr Ziel, die Grundsätze der Demokratie in alle Bereiche der Gesellschaft dringen zu lassen. Was ist denn Sozialdemokratie anderes als die fortschreitende und permanente Demokratisierung des gesellschaftlichen Lebens? Der Warnung Withalms vor einer uferlosen Demokratisierung stellte Kreisky entgegen, daß das Streben nach mehr Mitbestimmung, nach mehr Demokratie nicht der Ausdruck von Hemmungslosigkeit sei, sondern das Suchen nach neuen Ufern.  In einer Zeit, da der Staat übermächtig wird und seine Verwaltung kompliziert und undurchschaubar zu werden beginnt, bedarf es einer zusätzlichen Kontrolle und der Betonung des Grundsatzes, daß Staat und Verwaltung für die Menschen da sind und nicht umgekehrt.  Nach einem Bekenntnis zur Landesverteidigung forderte der SPVorsitzende ein Heer ohne Großmannsucht, das aus dem Partelenstreit herausgehalten werden soll und an dessen Spitze jemand steht, der sich in allen Bevölkerungskreisen Vertrauen erwerben kann.  Der Auftrag der Wähler  Zur bevorstehenden Wahl stellte Dr. Kreisky fest: Natürlich will die SPÖ von den Staatsbürgern einen, klaren Auftrag bekommen. Der eindeutigste Auftrag wäre die absolute Mehrheit. Darüber entscheidet niemand anderer als die österreichischen Wähler und Wählerinnen. Die Sozialisten werden aber, betonte Kreisky, jeden Auftrag, den ihnen die Wähler erteilen, nach bestem Wissen und Gewissen zu erfüllen trachten.

- Kreisky warned that an over‑powerful, opaque state requires stronger parliamentary control to ensure government serves the people.  
- He advocated for an army that operates without arrogance, independent of party conflicts, led by a widely trusted figure.  
- Regarding the upcoming election, he highlighted that the SP SPÖ seeks a clear voter mandate—ideally an absolute majority—and pledged to fulfill any mandate the electorate grants with full dedication.

Text: Parallel damit vollzieht sich eine Entwicklung, in der sich wirtschaftliche Macht und Eigentum voneinander lösen. Es entstehen neue Machtgruppen in der modernen Industriegesellschaft.   Mit Recht verlangt man überall dort, wo diese Erscheinung am sichtbarsten wird, neue Formen der Kontrolle dieser Konzentration der Macht in den Händen weniger. Die traditionellen Einrichtungen der Demokratie reichen nicht mehr aus, um diese Aufgabe zu erfüllen, und der immer drängender werdende Ruf nach Mitbestimmung ist der deutlichste Ausdruck dieses Unbehagens, von dem gerade die fortschrittlichsten Kräfte in den demokratischen Staaten erfüllt sind,  Nie zuvor war deshalb die Verwirklichung der grundlegenden Ideen der sozialen Demokratie, einer Demokratie, die alle gesellschaftlichen Bereiche unseres Lebens durchflutet, einer Demokratie, die über den rein politischen Raum hinaus auch die Bereiche des wirtschaftlichen und kulturellen Lebens zu durchdringen beginnt, von aktuellerer Bedeutung als heute.  Die Sozialistische Partei Österreichs ruft am Anfang dieses neuen Jahrzehnts vor allem die jungen Menschen auf, mit ihr an der Verwirklichung der Alternative für ein modernes Österreich zusammenzuwirken.  In zwei Monaten wird das Schicksal von Millionen Österreichern und Österreicherinnen in ihre Hand gegeben sein. Sie werden zu entscheiden haben zwischen jenen Parteien, die in einen selbstgefälligen und ideenlosen Konservativismus verstrickt sind, oder der Sozialistischen Partei Österreichs, die ein modernes Gemeinwesen verwirklichen will, in dem jeder das Recht auf eine gute Zukunft in Österreich hat, Leistung gewürdigt, Aufstieg ermöglicht und Sicherheit gewährleistet wird.  LETZTE VORBEREITUNGEN  Der Parteirat faßte am 12. Jänner 1970 die letzten Beschlüsse vor der Wahl am 1. März 1970. Die Kandidaten, die die SPÖ vorschlug, wurden nach einer breiten demokratischen Diskussion innerhalb der Partei aufgestellt.

The party has finalized its candidate list following internal democratic processes.

The text cites a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT policy proposals as models for the needed reforms, warning that without proper preparation Ireland risks losing the economic benefits of the Information Age.

- A modern, high‑quality, competitively priced communications infrastructure is deemed a national priority; however, OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with gaps in many areas.
- Telecom challenges include late EU‑wide mobile competition, an incomplete independent regulatory framework, delays in Telecom Eireann’s strategic alliance, and persistently high telecom costs that hinder business competitiveness.

Key initiatives include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with Telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—and integration of IT across all subjects. The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school computer access, including a national program to redistribute used devices and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre. It will also promote Irish-created education software and expand internet-based learning. While recognizing a modern communications infrastructure as a national priority, the plan notes that OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with persistent issues in mobile competition, regulatory delays, incomplete strategic alliances, and high costs affecting business competitiveness.

The text highlights a shift in industrial societies where economic power is separating from ownership, prompting demands for broader democratic participation, particularly from progressive movements. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs (SPÖ) champions extending democracy into economic and cultural realms, advocating for a society where all have fair recognition, opportunity, and security. With upcoming elections, voters face a choice between conservative inertia and SPÖ's vision of an inclusive, democratic future. Text: Equalise utility charges and other costs between rural and urban areas.  Develop a comprehensive programme to address the needs of our islands.  Acting while there is still time.  Fianna Fáil believe that the time has now come to create a radical new programme aimed at restoring the balance of our population between urban and rural areas.  If we do not act now, many rural communities will lose their viability and the depopulation trend will become irreversible. Meanwhile, the overbalanced growth of our large urban areas is creating social problems we can no longer ignore. Stimulating rural development will take some of the increasing pressure off our cities. Fianna Fáil’s rural development policy is based on recognising a number of basic realities.  - First, people will always go where the jobs are. Without adequate employment in rural areas, depopulation is inevitable.  - Second, agriculture can no longer on its own hope to sustain rural communities. Fianna Fáil’s policy is to keep as many farm families as possible on the land, but other forms of activity must exist to supplement the core contribution that agriculture makes. Increasingly, we see future job creation in rural areas in the services sector.  - Third, rural development cannot succeed fully until people in rural areas can get the same range and quality of services as in urban areas and at the same price. Too often, people living and working in rural areas do so under a handicap.  - Fourth, new technology particularly in communications now offers for the first time an opportunity to provide economically a wide range of services at truly local level. Technology now also makes it possible to run many more types of business from a rural base.  Eleven steps on the road to population stability.  Fianna Fáil in government will  1. Begin an energetic programme of localisation of state services that are now provided centrally. 

Summary:
chosen:
- Equalise utility charges and develop a comprehensive rural programme to restore population balance between urban and rural areas.  
- Rural depopulation threatens community viability unless jobs are created; agriculture alone cannot suffice, and services sector growth is key.  
- Rural residents must receive the same range, quality, and price of services as urban residents.  
- New communication technologies enable economically viable, locally delivered services and allow many businesses to operate from rural locations.  
- The policy will start by localising state services currently delivered centrally.

Text: Equalise utility charges and other costs between rural and urban areas.  Develop a comprehensive programme to address the needs of our islands.  Acting while there is still time.  Fianna Fáil believe that the time has now come to create a radical new programme aimed at restoring the balance of our population between urban and rural areas.  If we do not act now, many rural communities will lose their viability and the depopulation trend will become irreversible. Meanwhile, the overbalanced growth of our large urban areas is creating social problems we can no longer ignore. Stimulating rural development will take some of the increasing pressure off our cities. Fianna Fáil’s rural development policy is based on recognising a number of basic realities.  - First, people will always go where the jobs are. Without adequate employment in rural areas, depopulation is inevitable.  - Second, agriculture can no longer on its own hope to sustain rural communities. Fianna Fáil’s policy is to keep as many farm families as possible on the land, but other forms of activity must exist to supplement the core contribution that agriculture makes. Increasingly, we see future job creation in rural areas in the services sector.  - Third, rural development cannot succeed fully until people in rural areas can get the same range and quality of services as in urban areas and at the same price. Too often, people living and working in rural areas do so under a handicap.  - Fourth, new technology particularly in communications now offers for the first time an opportunity to provide economically a wide range of services at truly local level. Technology now also makes it possible to run many more types of business from a rural base.  Eleven steps on the road to population stability.  Fianna Fáil in government will  1. Begin an energetic programme of localisation of state services that are now provided centrally.

chosen:
- Equalise utility charges and develop a comprehensive rural programme to restore population balance between urban and rural areas.  
- Rural depopulation threatens community viability unless jobs are created; agriculture alone cannot suffice, and services sector growth is key.

- New communication technologies enable economically viable, locally delivered services and allow many businesses to operate from rural locations.  
- The policy will start by localising state services currently delivered centrally.

Text: The reason is that the new age offers us, for the first time since the Industrial Revolution, a way around the disadvantages we have always suffered because of our remote position on the periphery of Europe. In the Information Age, where we are will no longer matter. Ireland will be as well-placed as any country in a truly global market-place, if we have the right infrastructure in place. Indeed, because of the calibre of our people, Ireland is ideally positioned to become a leader in a world that will be dominated by knowledge industries. However, this opportunity must be grasped, the dividend from the Information Age will not come to us automatically. On the contrary: if we do not prepare properly, we will be left behind. If we fail to meet the challenge, the information age could undermine much of the economic success we have enjoyed so far. We must ready ourselves for the new era in two main ways. First, through the education system, preparing our people for a totally new way of doing things. Second, through our communications infrastructure, making sure that our people have full, low-cost access to the tools that make the new ways possible. In both these critical sectors, we are already behind. In both these areas the Rainbow Government has failed the people of Ireland. A recent survey showed Ireland to be, not in the vanguard of information age readiness where we could and should be, but in the third division of countries.  Educating for a new age.  In Fianna Fáil’s education Green Paper of 1992, we clearly signalled the coming significance of information technology in education. Fianna Fáil’s policy document on Information Technology in Education, published earlier this year, led the way in proposing a radical new departure. Since then the Rainbow Government has issued its own 5-year programme. Where appropriate or worthwhile, Fianna Fáil will incorporate elements of that programme into our own much more wide-ranging policy. 

Summary:
chosen: The passage argues that Ireland’s remote European position no longer limits its prospects in the Information Age, provided it invests in education and low‑cost communications infrastructure. It contends that these two sectors are essential for turning the new age into an opportunity and accuses the Rainbow Government of failing to act, leaving Ireland behind in global market readiness. The text cites a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT policy proposals as models for the needed reforms, warning that without proper preparation Ireland risks losing the economic benefits of the Information Age.

Text: Er teilte dem Parteirat mit, daß eine Finanzierungskommission gebildet Wurde, der Sozialisten angehören, die durch ihre Funktion im öffentlichen Leben und durch ihre Leistungen bewiesen haben, daß sie mit Geld umgehen können und die ihnen überantworteten Mittel gut verwalten. Diese Männer haben die sozialistischen Programme geprüft und in einem Gutachten als finanzierbar erklärt.  Der Kommission gehörten an: Die Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Doktor Schachner,  Suchanek und Dr. Vogl und die Bürgermeister von Landeshauptstädten Marek, Dipl.Ing. Scherbaum, Hillinger und Bäck. Diese Männer, betonte Kreisky, verwalten öffentliche Mittel von nahezu 30 Milliarden Schilling. Zusätzlich prüften und unterzeichneten das Gutachten noch der Generaldirektorstellvertreter der Nationalbank Dr. Kienzl sowie Dr. Veselsky und Direktor Dr. Uher (Länderbank).  Grundlage für die Politik der siebziger Jahre  Kreisky beschäftigte sich dann im einzelnen mit der Alternative der Sozialisten. Sie umfaßt Leitlinien der Außenpolitik, das Humanprogramm, das Kultur und Bildungsprogramm, das Wirtschaftsprogramm mit dem Verkehrskonzept und die Programme zur Verbesserung der staatlichen Einrichtungen Parlament, Justiz, Verwaltung und Bundesheer. Diese Programme bilden die Grundlage der Politik der Sozialistischen Partei für die siebziger Jahre.  Neuer Start für EFTAEWG  Zur Integrationspolitik sagte er, daß nun, da auch Frankreich sich vom altmodischen Gleichgewichtsdenken zu lösen beginnt, ein Fortschritt in der europäischen Integration erreicht werden könnte. Dabei sei zu berücksichtigen, daß es nicht nur die EWG und EFTA gibt, sondern innerhalb der EFTAStaaten, die den Beitritt zur EWG wollen und solche, die ein Nahverhältnis wünschen. Das Klügste wäre wohl, wenn sich die EWG und die EFTAStaaten einmal grundsätzlich zur wirtschaftlichen Zusammenarbeit bereit erklärten. Von hier weg sollten dann Lösungen für einen Ausgleich zwischen den beiden Wirtschaftsgemeinschaften gesucht werden.  

Summary:
chosen: A financing commission, composed of socialist officials (Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck) and auditors (Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher), was formed to audit and certify socialist programmes as financially viable, managing nearly 30 billion Schilling in public funds. These programmes cover foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative and military institutions, forming the basis of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda. Kreisky argues that, as France moves beyond traditional balance thinking, cooperation between the EWG and EFTA should be pursued, aiming to balance the economies of the two blocs.

Text:  Der Parteivorsitzende legte dann die Grundzüge der einzelnen Programme dar. Das Wirtschaftsprogramm sei heute wichtiger denn je, weil die ÖVP aus einem Propagandabedürfnis heraus eine Prosperitätseuphorie betreibe etwas, vor dem in anderen Ländern immer gewarnt werde. Di Hochkonjunktur überdecke falsche Wirtschaftsstrukturen jedoch nur zeitweise.  Für permanente Demokratisierung  Die Sozialdemokraten, setzte Kreisky fort, sind froh darüber, daß die Diskussion über die Demokratie nun überall in Gang gekommen ist, ist es doch ihr Ziel, die Grundsätze der Demokratie in alle Bereiche der Gesellschaft dringen zu lassen. Was ist denn Sozialdemokratie anderes als die fortschreitende und permanente Demokratisierung des gesellschaftlichen Lebens? Der Warnung Withalms vor einer uferlosen Demokratisierung stellte Kreisky entgegen, daß das Streben nach mehr Mitbestimmung, nach mehr Demokratie nicht der Ausdruck von Hemmungslosigkeit sei, sondern das Suchen nach neuen Ufern.  In einer Zeit, da der Staat übermächtig wird und seine Verwaltung kompliziert und undurchschaubar zu werden beginnt, bedarf es einer zusätzlichen Kontrolle und der Betonung des Grundsatzes, daß Staat und Verwaltung für die Menschen da sind und nicht umgekehrt.  Nach einem Bekenntnis zur Landesverteidigung forderte der SPVorsitzende ein Heer ohne Großmannsucht, das aus dem Partelenstreit herausgehalten werden soll und an dessen Spitze jemand steht, der sich in allen Bevölkerungskreisen Vertrauen erwerben kann.  Der Auftrag der Wähler  Zur bevorstehenden Wahl stellte Dr. Kreisky fest: Natürlich will die SPÖ von den Staatsbürgern einen, klaren Auftrag bekommen. Der eindeutigste Auftrag wäre die absolute Mehrheit. Darüber entscheidet niemand anderer als die österreichischen Wähler und Wählerinnen. Die Sozialisten werden aber, betonte Kreisky, jeden Auftrag, den ihnen die Wähler erteilen, nach bestem Wissen und Gewissen zu erfüllen trachten.

- Kreisky warned that an over‑powerful, opaque state requires stronger parliamentary control to ensure government serves the people.  
- He advocated for an army that operates without arrogance, independent of party conflicts, led by a widely trusted figure.  
- Regarding the upcoming election, he highlighted that the SP SPÖ seeks a clear voter mandate—ideally an absolute majority—and pledged to fulfill any mandate the electorate grants with full dedication.

To address the problems in inner city and other similar urban areas, we will employ community recreational facilitators to develop sport and leisure as an alternative and positive focus for young people.  - Appoint more physical education teachers in schools, where the emphasis should be on participation and fun rather than competition. We will build sport and physical training into the curriculum, and proficiency in it will be incorporated into the Junior and Leaving Certificates and the points system.  - Encourage partnerships between state and private sector funding in sport and leisure projects, and create tax reliefs and other incentives for private investors to stimulate maximum interest in the sector.  - Invite proposals for the construction of a 50-metre swimming pool, to serve both as an international arena and as a quality training facility. This project will be a headline for the type of joint venture between the public and private sectors which are necessary for to provide adequate facilities nationwide.  Balancing our population between urban and rural areas.  Fianna Fáil in government will  Initiate a comprehensive programme of rural development.  Take advantage of new technologies to encourage economic activity in rural areas.  Create development structures geared to the needs of rural development, and encourage rural enterprise by adjusting the social welfare means test.  Provide state services at local level, and accelerate the decentralisation of central services.  Provide equal quality in infrastructure and services throughout all regions.  

Summary:
chosen: The government plans to increase National Lottery funding for sport and appoint sport and leisure officers and community facilitators to expand access and engagement, particularly in urban areas. It aims to enhance physical education by integrating sport into school curricula and certification systems. Public-private partnerships will be incentivized through tax reliefs to develop sports infrastructure, including a proposed 50-metre swimming pool as a flagship joint venture. Additionally, a nationwide rural development program will promote decentralization, equal infrastructure quality, and rural enterprise through welfare adjustments and local service provision.

Text: Bundesparteivorstand  PARTEIRAT DER SPÖ: "LEISTUNG, AUFSTIEG, SICHERHEIT FÜR EIN MODERNES ÖSTERREICH"  "Leistung, Aufstieg, Sicherheit für ein modernes Österreich" war die Parole, unter der Parteirat am 22. November 1969 im Wiener Kongreßhaus als Arbeitskonferenz zusammentrat.  "Dieser Bundesparteirat wird in der Geschichte der Partei einen bedeutenden Platz einnehmen. er findet am Ende einer politischen Periode statt, die für die Sozialistische Partei schwer, aber auch fruchtbringend war", erklärte Nationalratspräsident Ing. Waldbrunner in seiner Begrüßungsansprache vor rund 500 Delegierten und Gästen. Waldbrunner zählte die lange Reihe der politischen Fehler und Unterlassungen der ÖVPRegierung.  Die Alternative der SPÖ liegt vor  Sodann sprach Parteivorsitzender Dr. Kreisky über die "Alternative für ein modernes Österreich". Er erinnerte einleitend daran, daß der Parteitag des Jahres 1958, der das Wiener Programm beschloß, vorsah, daß dieses Grundsatzprogramm durch konkrete Handlungsprogramme für die verschiedenen Bereiche ergänzt werden solle. Diese Programme liegen nun vor.  Kreisky dankte den 1400 Fachleuten sowie allen anderen Mitarbeitern an den Alternativprogrammen im Namen des Parteirats. Die ewige Forderung des politischen Gegners, eine Alternative zu präsentieren, sagte er weiter, ist nun aus der Debatte verschwunden. Der ÖVP ist nichts anderes übriggeblieben, als selbst in aller Hast ein Programm vorzulegen. Man müsse allerdings die Frage stellen, warum sich die Regierungspartei nicht schon früher damit beschäftigt habe. Zum ÖVPProgramm habe es auch keine Bedeckungsvorschläge gegeben.  SPProgramme sind finanzierbar  Damit leitete der Parteivorsitzende zur Frage der Finanzierung der SPProgramme über.

Text: Parallel damit vollzieht sich eine Entwicklung, in der sich wirtschaftliche Macht und Eigentum voneinander lösen. Es entstehen neue Machtgruppen in der modernen Industriegesellschaft.   Mit Recht verlangt man überall dort, wo diese Erscheinung am sichtbarsten wird, neue Formen der Kontrolle dieser Konzentration der Macht in den Händen weniger. Die traditionellen Einrichtungen der Demokratie reichen nicht mehr aus, um diese Aufgabe zu erfüllen, und der immer drängender werdende Ruf nach Mitbestimmung ist der deutlichste Ausdruck dieses Unbehagens, von dem gerade die fortschrittlichsten Kräfte in den demokratischen Staaten erfüllt sind,  Nie zuvor war deshalb die Verwirklichung der grundlegenden Ideen der sozialen Demokratie, einer Demokratie, die alle gesellschaftlichen Bereiche unseres Lebens durchflutet, einer Demokratie, die über den rein politischen Raum hinaus auch die Bereiche des wirtschaftlichen und kulturellen Lebens zu durchdringen beginnt, von aktuellerer Bedeutung als heute.  Die Sozialistische Partei Österreichs ruft am Anfang dieses neuen Jahrzehnts vor allem die jungen Menschen auf, mit ihr an der Verwirklichung der Alternative für ein modernes Österreich zusammenzuwirken.  In zwei Monaten wird das Schicksal von Millionen Österreichern und Österreicherinnen in ihre Hand gegeben sein. Sie werden zu entscheiden haben zwischen jenen Parteien, die in einen selbstgefälligen und ideenlosen Konservativismus verstrickt sind, oder der Sozialistischen Partei Österreichs, die ein modernes Gemeinwesen verwirklichen will, in dem jeder das Recht auf eine gute Zukunft in Österreich hat, Leistung gewürdigt, Aufstieg ermöglicht und Sicherheit gewährleistet wird.  LETZTE VORBEREITUNGEN  Der Parteirat faßte am 12. Jänner 1970 die letzten Beschlüsse vor der Wahl am 1. März 1970. Die Kandidaten, die die SPÖ vorschlug, wurden nach einer breiten demokratischen Diskussion innerhalb der Partei aufgestellt. 

Summary:
chosen: The text argues that modern industrial societies are undergoing a structural shift where economic power and ownership are separating, creating new power dynamics. This has exposed the limitations of traditional democratic institutions, prompting calls for expanded participation and control, especially from progressive forces in democratic nations. A central demand is extending democracy beyond politics into economic and cultural spheres. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs emphasizes this need and urges young people to join in building a modern Austria where everyone has the right to a good future, with fair recognition of effort, opportunity for advancement, and security. With elections approaching, voters are presented with a choice between conservative stagnation and the SPÖ's vision for a democratic, inclusive society. The party has finalized its candidate list following internal democratic processes.

We will set up a national system to distribute used computers from the private sector to schools, and upgrade the role of the National Information Technology in Education Centre in promoting it in schools.  - We will encourage and support the development of Irish-created education software, for both home and overseas markets.  - We will stimulate the full use of internet-based education projects.  Creating the right telecommunications infrastructure.  The key fact about the Information Age is that it is connected. Without the means to communicate instantly and cost-effectively, our human resources are powerless. For this reason, Fianna Fáil believe it is a vital national interest that Ireland has a state-of-the-art communications infrastructure that provides us with high-quality global access at keenly competitive rates. To reach our objectives, Ireland needs to be in the top quarter of developed countries for all the recognised service measures. But in fact, a recent OECD analysis showed that Ireland is in the top quarter for only two out of 13 measures. It is in the bottom quarter for four of the measures, and in the bottom half for seven out of the 13. We have a long way to go, and under the Rainbow Government progress in this vital sector has stagnated.  - Ireland was the last EU country to introduce competition in mobile phones.  - A proper independent regulatory framework is still not in place.  - Telecom Eireann’s strategic alliance has suffered grievously from prevarication and delay.  - Telecommunications costs are still far too high, making it more difficult for Irish business to compete.

- Telecom challenges include late EU‑wide mobile competition, an incomplete independent regulatory framework, delays in Telecom Eireann’s strategic alliance, and persistently high telecom costs that hinder business competitiveness.

The policy argues that Ireland's remote European location no longer limits its prospects if it invests in education and low-cost communications, citing a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT initiatives as models. It will also promote Irish-created education software and expand internet-based learning. Text: A socialist financing commission—including officials such as Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck, plus auditors Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher—was tasked with auditing and certifying socialist programmes as financially viable, managing roughly 30 billion Schilling. The programmes span foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative, and military institutions, forming the core of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda.

Kreisky, leader of the SP SPÖ, argues that France’s shift away from traditional balance thinking requires cooperation between the EWG and EFTA to equilibrate the two blocs. He critiques the ÖVP’s "prosperity euphoria" as temporary and structurally flawed, promoting “permanent democratization” and stronger parliamentary oversight of a powerful, opaque state. He envisions an army that operates without arrogance and independently of party conflicts, and he seeks a clear voter mandate—ideally an absolute majority—to implement his reforms.

The party’s broader platform stresses that human fate depends on social order, criticizes governments for causing conflict and starvation despite technological progress, warns against corporate concentration, and calls for peaceful conflict resolution and equitable use of technological advances.

The text highlights a shift in industrial societies where economic power is separating from ownership, prompting demands for broader democratic participation, particularly from progressive movements. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs (SPÖ) champions extending democracy into economic and cultural realms, advocating for a society where all have fair recognition, opportunity, and security. With upcoming elections, voters face a choice between conservative inertia and SPÖ's vision of an inclusive, democratic future. SPÖ has finalized its National Council candidate lists across all 25 constituencies through internal democratic processes, with an age distribution showing 6.06% under 30, 17.88% aged 30–41, 50.90% aged 40–50, 21.82% aged 50–60, and 3.34% over 60. These lists have been unanimously approved and confirmed for all constituencies and sub-divisions, reflecting broad party support.

Summary:
chosen: The SPÖ established a socialist financing commission, led by figures including Kreisky and regional officials, to audit and certify around 30 billion Schilling in socialist programs covering foreign policy, culture, economic planning, and institutional reforms. Kreisky advocated for expanded democratic control, criticizing conservative economic policies and calling for an absolute mandate to implement structural reforms, including parliamentary oversight and military independence. The party promoted a vision of democracy extending into economic and cultural spheres, with a candidate platform reflecting broad internal support and a commitment to equitable, peaceful progress. Voter choice in upcoming elections was framed as a contrast between conservative inertia and SPÖ’s inclusive, reform-oriented agenda.

Text: Equalise utility charges and other costs between rural and urban areas.  Develop a comprehensive programme to address the needs of our islands.  Acting while there is still time.  Fianna Fáil believe that the time has now come to create a radical new programme aimed at restoring the balance of our population between urban and rural areas.  If we do not act now, many rural communities will lose their viability and the depopulation trend will become irreversible. Meanwhile, the overbalanced growth of our large urban areas is creating social problems we can no longer ignore. Stimulating rural development will take some of the increasing pressure off our cities. Fianna Fáil’s rural development policy is based on recognising a number of basic realities.  - First, people will always go where the jobs are. Without adequate employment in rural areas, depopulation is inevitable.  - Second, agriculture can no longer on its own hope to sustain rural communities. Fianna Fáil’s policy is to keep as many farm families as possible on the land, but other forms of activity must exist to supplement the core contribution that agriculture makes. Increasingly, we see future job creation in rural areas in the services sector.  - Third, rural development cannot succeed fully until people in rural areas can get the same range and quality of services as in urban areas and at the same price. Too often, people living and working in rural areas do so under a handicap.  - Fourth, new technology particularly in communications now offers for the first time an opportunity to provide economically a wide range of services at truly local level. Technology now also makes it possible to run many more types of business from a rural base.  Eleven steps on the road to population stability.  Fianna Fáil in government will  1. Begin an energetic programme of localisation of state services that are now provided centrally. 

Summary:
chosen:
- Equalise utility charges and develop a comprehensive rural programme to restore population balance between urban and rural areas.  
- Rural depopulation threatens community viability unless jobs are created; agriculture alone cannot suffice, and services sector growth is key.  
- Rural residents must receive the same range, quality, and price of services as urban residents.  
- New communication technologies enable economically viable, locally delivered services and allow many businesses to operate from rural locations.  
- The policy will start by localising state services currently delivered centrally.

Text: The reason is that the new age offers us, for the first time since the Industrial Revolution, a way around the disadvantages we have always suffered because of our remote position on the periphery of Europe. In the Information Age, where we are will no longer matter. Ireland will be as well-placed as any country in a truly global market-place, if we have the right infrastructure in place. Indeed, because of the calibre of our people, Ireland is ideally positioned to become a leader in a world that will be dominated by knowledge industries. Text: Er teilte dem Parteirat mit, daß eine Finanzierungskommission gebildet Wurde, der Sozialisten angehören, die durch ihre Funktion im öffentlichen Leben und durch ihre Leistungen bewiesen haben, daß sie mit Geld umgehen können und die ihnen überantworteten Mittel gut verwalten. Diese Männer haben die sozialistischen Programme geprüft und in einem Gutachten als finanzierbar erklärt.  Der Kommission gehörten an: Die Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Doktor Schachner,  Suchanek und Dr. Vogl und die Bürgermeister von Landeshauptstädten Marek, Dipl.Ing. Scherbaum, Hillinger und Bäck. Diese Männer, betonte Kreisky, verwalten öffentliche Mittel von nahezu 30 Milliarden Schilling. Zusätzlich prüften und unterzeichneten das Gutachten noch der Generaldirektorstellvertreter der Nationalbank Dr. Kienzl sowie Dr. Veselsky und Direktor Dr. Uher (Länderbank).  Grundlage für die Politik der siebziger Jahre  Kreisky beschäftigte sich dann im einzelnen mit der Alternative der Sozialisten. Sie umfaßt Leitlinien der Außenpolitik, das Humanprogramm, das Kultur und Bildungsprogramm, das Wirtschaftsprogramm mit dem Verkehrskonzept und die Programme zur Verbesserung der staatlichen Einrichtungen Parlament, Justiz, Verwaltung und Bundesheer. Diese Programme bilden die Grundlage der Politik der Sozialistischen Partei für die siebziger Jahre.  Neuer Start für EFTAEWG  Zur Integrationspolitik sagte er, daß nun, da auch Frankreich sich vom altmodischen Gleichgewichtsdenken zu lösen beginnt, ein Fortschritt in der europäischen Integration erreicht werden könnte. Dabei sei zu berücksichtigen, daß es nicht nur die EWG und EFTA gibt, sondern innerhalb der EFTAStaaten, die den Beitritt zur EWG wollen und solche, die ein Nahverhältnis wünschen. Das Klügste wäre wohl, wenn sich die EWG und die EFTAStaaten einmal grundsätzlich zur wirtschaftlichen Zusammenarbeit bereit erklärten. Von hier weg sollten dann Lösungen für einen Ausgleich zwischen den beiden Wirtschaftsgemeinschaften gesucht werden.  

Summary:
chosen: A financing commission, composed of socialist officials (Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck) and auditors (Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher), was formed to audit and certify socialist programmes as financially viable, managing nearly 30 billion Schilling in public funds. These programmes cover foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative and military institutions, forming the basis of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda. Kreisky argues that, as France moves beyond traditional balance thinking, cooperation between the EWG and EFTA should be pursued, aiming to balance the economies of the two blocs.

Text: We will make information technology an education priority.  Fianna Fáil in government will ensure that every young person is computer literate by the end of their school career. We will make information technology a fully integrated and fully available component of the Irish education system.  - We will put in place a 5-year programme of research between third-level colleges and business.  - We will establish a new body combining the HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas and IBEC to co-ordinate national up-skilling in new technologies.  - We will consider setting up a Science, Technology and Innovation forum, to promote Ireland as a centre of scientific and technological excellence.  Towards computer literacy in five years.  Fianna Fáil will put in place a 5-year plan, at the end of which every classroom in the country will have a multimedia computer, with direct access to the internet. Within two years, every school will have that access. This will apply to primary schools as well as secondary, since we believe that computer literacy must begin early. Elements of Fianna Fáil’s information age plan:  - We will provide 100% funding to get information technology into schools in disadvantaged areas. This is critical to avoid opening up a new field of disadvantage, since students in these schools rarely have access to a computer at home.  - We will make a special deal with telecom Eireann for separate phone lines and low-cost internet access to schools.  - We will give an annual budget to each school, for computer maintenance and running costs.  - We will provide comprehensive in-career training programmes for teachers, so they can not only use computers effectively but also can integrate the technology fully into their teaching in every curriculum area. All training for new teachers will give a high priority to using Information Technology in teaching.

Text:  Der Parteivorsitzende legte dann die Grundzüge der einzelnen Programme dar. Das Wirtschaftsprogramm sei heute wichtiger denn je, weil die ÖVP aus einem Propagandabedürfnis heraus eine Prosperitätseuphorie betreibe etwas, vor dem in anderen Ländern immer gewarnt werde. Di Hochkonjunktur überdecke falsche Wirtschaftsstrukturen jedoch nur zeitweise.  Für permanente Demokratisierung  Die Sozialdemokraten, setzte Kreisky fort, sind froh darüber, daß die Diskussion über die Demokratie nun überall in Gang gekommen ist, ist es doch ihr Ziel, die Grundsätze der Demokratie in alle Bereiche der Gesellschaft dringen zu lassen. Was ist denn Sozialdemokratie anderes als die fortschreitende und permanente Demokratisierung des gesellschaftlichen Lebens? Der Warnung Withalms vor einer uferlosen Demokratisierung stellte Kreisky entgegen, daß das Streben nach mehr Mitbestimmung, nach mehr Demokratie nicht der Ausdruck von Hemmungslosigkeit sei, sondern das Suchen nach neuen Ufern.  In einer Zeit, da der Staat übermächtig wird und seine Verwaltung kompliziert und undurchschaubar zu werden beginnt, bedarf es einer zusätzlichen Kontrolle und der Betonung des Grundsatzes, daß Staat und Verwaltung für die Menschen da sind und nicht umgekehrt.  Nach einem Bekenntnis zur Landesverteidigung forderte der SPVorsitzende ein Heer ohne Großmannsucht, das aus dem Partelenstreit herausgehalten werden soll und an dessen Spitze jemand steht, der sich in allen Bevölkerungskreisen Vertrauen erwerben kann.  Der Auftrag der Wähler  Zur bevorstehenden Wahl stellte Dr. Kreisky fest: Natürlich will die SPÖ von den Staatsbürgern einen, klaren Auftrag bekommen. Der eindeutigste Auftrag wäre die absolute Mehrheit. Darüber entscheidet niemand anderer als die österreichischen Wähler und Wählerinnen. Die Sozialisten werden aber, betonte Kreisky, jeden Auftrag, den ihnen die Wähler erteilen, nach bestem Wissen und Gewissen zu erfüllen trachten.

Die Sozialistische Partei wandte sich zum Jahreswechsel 1969/70 mit folgendem Aufruf an alle Österreicher und Österreicherinnen:  "Die Sozialistische Partei wünscht aus Anlaß der Jahreswende, die diesmal auch ein neues Ja zehnt einleitet, allen Österreichern und Österreicherinnen ein gutes neues Jahr. Das Schicksal jedes Menschen, jeder Familie hängt in sehr hohem, geradezu in entscheidendem Maße von der sozialen Ordnung ab, in der sie leben. In einer Zeit, in der es des Menschen Geist und seiner Kraft gelungen ist, diesen Planeten zu verlassen und auf einein neuen Fuß zu fassen, ist es um so unverständlicher, daß es nicht gelingt, die Probleme, die unser Leben auf der Erde überschatten, zu lösen.  Täglich müssen Menschen sterben, weil über sie herrschende Regierungen sie in kriegerische Auseinandersetzungen hineintreiben, statt daß von diesen Regierungen verlangt wird, daß sie altes unternehmen mögen, um Konflikte auf friedliche Art auszutragen.   TÄGLICH müssen Millionen Menschen verhungern, obwohl es Länder gibt, in denen der Oberfluß zur Sorge und Plage wird. Diese modernen Industriestaaten bedienen sich neuer Methoden der Warenerzeugung und vermögen mit neuen Maschinen nicht nur die Kraft des Menschen, sondern auch sein Denk und Erinnerungsvermögen zu vervielfachen. Denn nie vorher waren die technischen und materiellen Voraussetzungen hiefür in GLEICHER WEISE GEGEBEN.  Aber in der modernen Industriegesellschaft vollzieht sich in immer deutlicherer  Weise ein Konzentrationsprozeß, der gekennzeichnet ist durch neue Formen der Zusammenschlüsse von Unternehmungen.

Text: Parallel damit vollzieht sich eine Entwicklung, in der sich wirtschaftliche Macht und Eigentum voneinander lösen. Es entstehen neue Machtgruppen in der modernen Industriegesellschaft.   Mit Recht verlangt man überall dort, wo diese Erscheinung am sichtbarsten wird, neue Formen der Kontrolle dieser Konzentration der Macht in den Händen weniger. Die traditionellen Einrichtungen der Demokratie reichen nicht mehr aus, um diese Aufgabe zu erfüllen, und der immer drängender werdende Ruf nach Mitbestimmung ist der deutlichste Ausdruck dieses Unbehagens, von dem gerade die fortschrittlichsten Kräfte in den demokratischen Staaten erfüllt sind,  Nie zuvor war deshalb die Verwirklichung der grundlegenden Ideen der sozialen Demokratie, einer Demokratie, die alle gesellschaftlichen Bereiche unseres Lebens durchflutet, einer Demokratie, die über den rein politischen Raum hinaus auch die Bereiche des wirtschaftlichen und kulturellen Lebens zu durchdringen beginnt, von aktuellerer Bedeutung als heute.  Die Sozialistische Partei Österreichs ruft am Anfang dieses neuen Jahrzehnts vor allem die jungen Menschen auf, mit ihr an der Verwirklichung der Alternative für ein modernes Österreich zusammenzuwirken.  In zwei Monaten wird das Schicksal von Millionen Österreichern und Österreicherinnen in ihre Hand gegeben sein. Sie werden zu entscheiden haben zwischen jenen Parteien, die in einen selbstgefälligen und ideenlosen Konservativismus verstrickt sind, oder der Sozialistischen Partei Österreichs, die ein modernes Gemeinwesen verwirklichen will, in dem jeder das Recht auf eine gute Zukunft in Österreich hat, Leistung gewürdigt, Aufstieg ermöglicht und Sicherheit gewährleistet wird.  LETZTE VORBEREITUNGEN  Der Parteirat faßte am 12. Jänner 1970 die letzten Beschlüsse vor der Wahl am 1. März 1970. Die Kandidaten, die die SPÖ vorschlug, wurden nach einer breiten demokratischen Diskussion innerhalb der Partei aufgestellt.

chosen: The text argues that modern industrial societies are undergoing a structural shift where economic power and ownership are separating, creating new power dynamics. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs emphasizes this need and urges young people to join in building a modern Austria where everyone has the right to a good future, with fair recognition of effort, opportunity for advancement, and security. With elections approaching, voters are presented with a choice between conservative stagnation and the SPÖ's vision for a democratic, inclusive society. The party has finalized its candidate list following internal democratic processes.

Text: Fianna Fáil proposes making information technology a core component of Irish education by establishing a 5-year plan to ensure all students become computer literate. The plan includes integrating IT into the national curriculum from primary through secondary levels, with all classrooms equipped with multimedia computers and internet access within two years, and full implementation within five years. It establishes a coordinating body combining HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas, and IBEC to align national up-skilling efforts, and proposes a Science, Technology and Innovation forum to position Ireland as a technological hub. Key actions include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, and comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—focused on effective IT integration across all subjects.

- The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school access to computers, including a national program to redistribute used private‑sector computers and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre.
- It will promote Irish‑created education software and expand internet‑based learning projects.
- A modern, high‑quality, competitively priced communications infrastructure is deemed a national priority; however, OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with gaps in many areas.
- Telecom challenges include late EU‑wide mobile competition, an incomplete independent regulatory framework, delays in Telecom Eireann’s strategic alliance, and persistently high telecom costs that hinder business competitiveness.

Summary:
chosen: Fianna Fáil proposes a 5-year plan to embed information technology into Ireland's education system by making it a core component from primary through secondary levels, ensuring all classrooms are equipped with multimedia computers and internet access. The plan involves establishing a coordinating body comprising HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas, and IBEC to align national up-skilling efforts, and launching a Science, Technology and Innovation forum to position Ireland as a technological hub. Key initiatives include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with Telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—and integration of IT across all subjects. The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school computer access, including a national program to redistribute used devices and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre. It will also promote Irish-created education software and expand internet-based learning. While recognizing a modern communications infrastructure as a national priority, the plan notes that OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with persistent issues in mobile competition, regulatory delays, incomplete strategic alliances, and high costs affecting business competitiveness.

Text: The Irish government proposes a comprehensive energy and Information Age strategy involving mandatory disclosure of vehicle fuel costs, energy-efficiency-linked tax incentives, a National Energy Trust, stricter building regulations, and grants for high-efficiency homebuyers. It also outlines a 5-year plan to equip all classrooms with computers and internet, improve telecom infrastructure through Telecom Éireann reforms, and invest in tourism, agriculture, marine resources, and a dynamic public sector. The policy argues that Ireland's remote European location no longer limits its prospects if it invests in education and low-cost communications, citing a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT initiatives as models. It criticizes past government inaction, particularly the Rainbow Government, for failing to prepare Ireland for the Information Age, warning that without reform, the country risks missing the economic benefits of this era.

Fianna Fáil proposes a 5-year plan to embed information technology into Ireland's education system by making it a core component from primary through secondary levels, ensuring all classrooms are equipped with multimedia computers and internet access. The plan involves establishing a coordinating body comprising HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas, and IBEC to align national up-skilling efforts, and launching a Science, Technology and Innovation forum to position Ireland as a technological hub. Key initiatives include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with Telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—and integration of IT across all subjects. The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school computer access, including a national program to redistribute used devices and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre. It will also promote Irish-created education software and expand internet-based learning. While recognizing a modern communications infrastructure as a national priority, the plan notes that OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with persistent issues in mobile competition, regulatory delays, incomplete strategic alliances, and high costs affecting business competitiveness.

Text: A socialist financing commission—including officials such as Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck, plus auditors Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher—was tasked with auditing and certifying socialist programmes as financially viable, managing roughly 30 billion Schilling. The programmes span foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative, and military institutions, forming the core of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda.

Kreisky, leader of the SP SPÖ, argues that France’s shift away from traditional balance thinking requires cooperation between the EWG and EFTA to equilibrate the two blocs. He critiques the ÖVP’s "prosperity euphoria" as temporary and structurally flawed, promoting “permanent democratization” and stronger parliamentary oversight of a powerful, opaque state. He envisions an army that operates without arrogance and independently of party conflicts, and he seeks a clear voter mandate—ideally an absolute majority—to implement his reforms.

The party’s broader platform stresses that human fate depends on social order, criticizes governments for causing conflict and starvation despite technological progress, warns against corporate concentration, and calls for peaceful conflict resolution and equitable use of technological advances.

The text highlights a shift in industrial societies where economic power is separating from ownership, prompting demands for broader democratic participation, particularly from progressive movements. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs (SPÖ) champions extending democracy into economic and cultural realms, advocating for a society where all have fair recognition, opportunity, and security. With upcoming elections, voters face a choice between conservative inertia and SPÖ's vision of an inclusive, democratic future. SPÖ has finalized its National Council candidate lists across all 25 constituencies through internal democratic processes, with an age distribution showing 6.06% under 30, 17.88% aged 30–41, 50.90% aged 40–50, 21.82% aged 50–60, and 3.34% over 60. These lists have been unanimously approved and confirmed for all constituencies and sub-divisions, reflecting broad party support.

The party promoted a vision of democracy extending into economic and cultural spheres, with a candidate platform reflecting broad internal support and a commitment to equitable, peaceful progress. Voter choice in upcoming elections was framed as a contrast between conservative inertia and SPÖ’s inclusive, reform-oriented agenda.

Text: Equalise utility charges and other costs between rural and urban areas.  Develop a comprehensive programme to address the needs of our islands.  Acting while there is still time.  Fianna Fáil believe that the time has now come to create a radical new programme aimed at restoring the balance of our population between urban and rural areas.  If we do not act now, many rural communities will lose their viability and the depopulation trend will become irreversible. Meanwhile, the overbalanced growth of our large urban areas is creating social problems we can no longer ignore. Stimulating rural development will take some of the increasing pressure off our cities. Fianna Fáil’s rural development policy is based on recognising a number of basic realities.  - First, people will always go where the jobs are. Without adequate employment in rural areas, depopulation is inevitable.  - Second, agriculture can no longer on its own hope to sustain rural communities. Fianna Fáil’s policy is to keep as many farm families as possible on the land, but other forms of activity must exist to supplement the core contribution that agriculture makes. Increasingly, we see future job creation in rural areas in the services sector.  - Third, rural development cannot succeed fully until people in rural areas can get the same range and quality of services as in urban areas and at the same price. Too often, people living and working in rural areas do so under a handicap.  - Fourth, new technology particularly in communications now offers for the first time an opportunity to provide economically a wide range of services at truly local level. Technology now also makes it possible to run many more types of business from a rural base.  Eleven steps on the road to population stability.  Fianna Fáil in government will  1. Begin an energetic programme of localisation of state services that are now provided centrally. 

Summary:
chosen:
- Equalise utility charges and develop a comprehensive rural programme to restore population balance between urban and rural areas.  
- Rural depopulation threatens community viability unless jobs are created; agriculture alone cannot suffice, and services sector growth is key.  
- Rural residents must receive the same range, quality, and price of services as urban residents.  
- New communication technologies enable economically viable, locally delivered services and allow many businesses to operate from rural locations.  
- The policy will start by localising state services currently delivered centrally.

Text: The reason is that the new age offers us, for the first time since the Industrial Revolution, a way around the disadvantages we have always suffered because of our remote position on the periphery of Europe. In the Information Age, where we are will no longer matter. Ireland will be as well-placed as any country in a truly global market-place, if we have the right infrastructure in place. Indeed, because of the calibre of our people, Ireland is ideally positioned to become a leader in a world that will be dominated by knowledge industries. However, this opportunity must be grasped, the dividend from the Information Age will not come to us automatically. On the contrary: if we do not prepare properly, we will be left behind. If we fail to meet the challenge, the information age could undermine much of the economic success we have enjoyed so far. We must ready ourselves for the new era in two main ways. First, through the education system, preparing our people for a totally new way of doing things. Second, through our communications infrastructure, making sure that our people have full, low-cost access to the tools that make the new ways possible. In both these critical sectors, we are already behind. In both these areas the Rainbow Government has failed the people of Ireland. A recent survey showed Ireland to be, not in the vanguard of information age readiness where we could and should be, but in the third division of countries.  Educating for a new age.  In Fianna Fáil’s education Green Paper of 1992, we clearly signalled the coming significance of information technology in education. Fianna Fáil’s policy document on Information Technology in Education, published earlier this year, led the way in proposing a radical new departure. Since then the Rainbow Government has issued its own 5-year programme. Where appropriate or worthwhile, Fianna Fáil will incorporate elements of that programme into our own much more wide-ranging policy. 

Summary:
chosen: The passage argues that Ireland’s remote European position no longer limits its prospects in the Information Age, provided it invests in education and low‑cost communications infrastructure. It contends that these two sectors are essential for turning the new age into an opportunity and accuses the Rainbow Government of failing to act, leaving Ireland behind in global market readiness. The text cites a 1992 Fianna Fáil education Green Paper and recent IT policy proposals as models for the needed reforms, warning that without proper preparation Ireland risks losing the economic benefits of the Information Age.

Text: The reason is that the new age offers us, for the first time since the Industrial Revolution, a way around the disadvantages we have always suffered because of our remote position on the periphery of Europe. In the Information Age, where we are will no longer matter. Ireland will be as well-placed as any country in a truly global market-place, if we have the right infrastructure in place. Indeed, because of the calibre of our people, Ireland is ideally positioned to become a leader in a world that will be dominated by knowledge industries. If we fail to meet the challenge, the information age could undermine much of the economic success we have enjoyed so far. We must ready ourselves for the new era in two main ways. First, through the education system, preparing our people for a totally new way of doing things. Second, through our communications infrastructure, making sure that our people have full, low-cost access to the tools that make the new ways possible. In Fianna Fáil’s education Green Paper of 1992, we clearly signalled the coming significance of information technology in education. Fianna Fáil’s policy document on Information Technology in Education, published earlier this year, led the way in proposing a radical new departure. Where appropriate or worthwhile, Fianna Fáil will incorporate elements of that programme into our own much more wide-ranging policy.

Text: Er teilte dem Parteirat mit, daß eine Finanzierungskommission gebildet Wurde, der Sozialisten angehören, die durch ihre Funktion im öffentlichen Leben und durch ihre Leistungen bewiesen haben, daß sie mit Geld umgehen können und die ihnen überantworteten Mittel gut verwalten. Diese Männer haben die sozialistischen Programme geprüft und in einem Gutachten als finanzierbar erklärt.  Der Kommission gehörten an: Die Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Doktor Schachner,  Suchanek und Dr. Vogl und die Bürgermeister von Landeshauptstädten Marek, Dipl.Ing. Scherbaum, Hillinger und Bäck. Diese Männer, betonte Kreisky, verwalten öffentliche Mittel von nahezu 30 Milliarden Schilling. Zusätzlich prüften und unterzeichneten das Gutachten noch der Generaldirektorstellvertreter der Nationalbank Dr. Kienzl sowie Dr. Veselsky und Direktor Dr. Uher (Länderbank).  Grundlage für die Politik der siebziger Jahre  Kreisky beschäftigte sich dann im einzelnen mit der Alternative der Sozialisten. Sie umfaßt Leitlinien der Außenpolitik, das Humanprogramm, das Kultur und Bildungsprogramm, das Wirtschaftsprogramm mit dem Verkehrskonzept und die Programme zur Verbesserung der staatlichen Einrichtungen Parlament, Justiz, Verwaltung und Bundesheer. Diese Programme bilden die Grundlage der Politik der Sozialistischen Partei für die siebziger Jahre.  Neuer Start für EFTAEWG  Zur Integrationspolitik sagte er, daß nun, da auch Frankreich sich vom altmodischen Gleichgewichtsdenken zu lösen beginnt, ein Fortschritt in der europäischen Integration erreicht werden könnte. Dabei sei zu berücksichtigen, daß es nicht nur die EWG und EFTA gibt, sondern innerhalb der EFTAStaaten, die den Beitritt zur EWG wollen und solche, die ein Nahverhältnis wünschen. Das Klügste wäre wohl, wenn sich die EWG und die EFTAStaaten einmal grundsätzlich zur wirtschaftlichen Zusammenarbeit bereit erklärten. Von hier weg sollten dann Lösungen für einen Ausgleich zwischen den beiden Wirtschaftsgemeinschaften gesucht werden.  

Summary:
chosen: A financing commission, composed of socialist officials (Landesregierungsmitglieder Slavik, Dr. Schachner, Suchanek, Dr. Vogl and mayors Marek, Scherbaum, Hillinger, Bäck) and auditors (Dr. Kienzl, Dr. Veselsky, Dr. Uher), was formed to audit and certify socialist programmes as financially viable, managing nearly 30 billion Schilling in public funds. These programmes cover foreign policy, a Humanprogramm, cultural and education initiatives, an economic plan with a transport concept, and reforms of parliamentary, judicial, administrative and military institutions, forming the basis of the Socialist Party’s 1970s agenda. Kreisky argues that, as France moves beyond traditional balance thinking, cooperation between the EWG and EFTA should be pursued, aiming to balance the economies of the two blocs.

We will make information technology a fully integrated and fully available component of the Irish education system.  - We will put in place a 5-year programme of research between third-level colleges and business.  - We will establish a new body combining the HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas and IBEC to co-ordinate national up-skilling in new technologies.  - We will consider setting up a Science, Technology and Innovation forum, to promote Ireland as a centre of scientific and technological excellence. Elements of Fianna Fáil’s information age plan:  - We will provide 100% funding to get information technology into schools in disadvantaged areas. All training for new teachers will give a high priority to using Information Technology in teaching.

Di Hochkonjunktur überdecke falsche Wirtschaftsstrukturen jedoch nur zeitweise.  Für permanente Demokratisierung  Die Sozialdemokraten, setzte Kreisky fort, sind froh darüber, daß die Diskussion über die Demokratie nun überall in Gang gekommen ist, ist es doch ihr Ziel, die Grundsätze der Demokratie in alle Bereiche der Gesellschaft dringen zu lassen. Der Warnung Withalms vor einer uferlosen Demokratisierung stellte Kreisky entgegen, daß das Streben nach mehr Mitbestimmung, nach mehr Demokratie nicht der Ausdruck von Hemmungslosigkeit sei, sondern das Suchen nach neuen Ufern.  In einer Zeit, da der Staat übermächtig wird und seine Verwaltung kompliziert und undurchschaubar zu werden beginnt, bedarf es einer zusätzlichen Kontrolle und der Betonung des Grundsatzes, daß Staat und Verwaltung für die Menschen da sind und nicht umgekehrt. Der Auftrag der Wähler  Zur bevorstehenden Wahl stellte Dr. Kreisky fest: Natürlich will die SPÖ von den Staatsbürgern einen, klaren Auftrag bekommen. Der eindeutigste Auftrag wäre die absolute Mehrheit. Darüber entscheidet niemand anderer als die österreichischen Wähler und Wählerinnen. Text: Parallel damit vollzieht sich eine Entwicklung, in der sich wirtschaftliche Macht und Eigentum voneinander lösen. Es entstehen neue Machtgruppen in der modernen Industriegesellschaft.   Mit Recht verlangt man überall dort, wo diese Erscheinung am sichtbarsten wird, neue Formen der Kontrolle dieser Konzentration der Macht in den Händen weniger. Die traditionellen Einrichtungen der Demokratie reichen nicht mehr aus, um diese Aufgabe zu erfüllen, und der immer drängender werdende Ruf nach Mitbestimmung ist der deutlichste Ausdruck dieses Unbehagens, von dem gerade die fortschrittlichsten Kräfte in den demokratischen Staaten erfüllt sind,  Nie zuvor war deshalb die Verwirklichung der grundlegenden Ideen der sozialen Demokratie, einer Demokratie, die alle gesellschaftlichen Bereiche unseres Lebens durchflutet, einer Demokratie, die über den rein politischen Raum hinaus auch die Bereiche des wirtschaftlichen und kulturellen Lebens zu durchdringen beginnt, von aktuellerer Bedeutung als heute.  Die Sozialistische Partei Österreichs ruft am Anfang dieses neuen Jahrzehnts vor allem die jungen Menschen auf, mit ihr an der Verwirklichung der Alternative für ein modernes Österreich zusammenzuwirken.  In zwei Monaten wird das Schicksal von Millionen Österreichern und Österreicherinnen in ihre Hand gegeben sein. Sie werden zu entscheiden haben zwischen jenen Parteien, die in einen selbstgefälligen und ideenlosen Konservativismus verstrickt sind, oder der Sozialistischen Partei Österreichs, die ein modernes Gemeinwesen verwirklichen will, in dem jeder das Recht auf eine gute Zukunft in Österreich hat, Leistung gewürdigt, Aufstieg ermöglicht und Sicherheit gewährleistet wird.  LETZTE VORBEREITUNGEN  Der Parteirat faßte am 12. Jänner 1970 die letzten Beschlüsse vor der Wahl am 1. März 1970. Die Kandidaten, die die SPÖ vorschlug, wurden nach einer breiten demokratischen Diskussion innerhalb der Partei aufgestellt.

chosen: The text argues that modern industrial societies are undergoing a structural shift where economic power and ownership are separating, creating new power dynamics. This has exposed the limitations of traditional democratic institutions, prompting calls for expanded participation and control, especially from progressive forces in democratic nations. A central demand is extending democracy beyond politics into economic and cultural spheres. The Sozialistische Partei Österreichs emphasizes this need and urges young people to join in building a modern Austria where everyone has the right to a good future, with fair recognition of effort, opportunity for advancement, and security. With elections approaching, voters are presented with a choice between conservative stagnation and the SPÖ's vision for a democratic, inclusive society. The party has finalized its candidate list following internal democratic processes.

Text: Fianna Fáil proposes making information technology a core component of Irish education by establishing a 5-year plan to ensure all students become computer literate. The plan includes integrating IT into the national curriculum from primary through secondary levels, with all classrooms equipped with multimedia computers and internet access within two years, and full implementation within five years. It establishes a coordinating body combining HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas, and IBEC to align national up-skilling efforts, and proposes a Science, Technology and Innovation forum to position Ireland as a technological hub. Key actions include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, and comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—focused on effective IT integration across all subjects.

- The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school access to computers, including a national program to redistribute used private‑sector computers and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre.
- It will promote Irish‑created education software and expand internet‑based learning projects.
- A modern, high‑quality, competitively priced communications infrastructure is deemed a national priority; however, OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with gaps in many areas.
- Telecom challenges include late EU‑wide mobile competition, an incomplete independent regulatory framework, delays in Telecom Eireann’s strategic alliance, and persistently high telecom costs that hinder business competitiveness.

Summary:
chosen: Fianna Fáil proposes a 5-year plan to embed information technology into Ireland's education system by making it a core component from primary through secondary levels, ensuring all classrooms are equipped with multimedia computers and internet access. The plan involves establishing a coordinating body comprising HEA, third-level institutions, IDA, Forbairt, Forfas, and IBEC to align national up-skilling efforts, and launching a Science, Technology and Innovation forum to position Ireland as a technological hub. Key initiatives include full funding for IT access in disadvantaged schools, a dedicated agreement with Telecom Eireann for low-cost internet and phone lines, annual school budgets for maintenance, comprehensive teacher training—including pre-service education—and integration of IT across all subjects. The government will partner with the private sector and the Department of Education to accelerate school computer access, including a national program to redistribute used devices and strengthen the National IT in Education Centre. It will also promote Irish-created education software and expand internet-based learning. While recognizing a modern communications infrastructure as a national priority, the plan notes that OECD data shows Ireland ranks in the top quarter for only 2 of 13 telecom metrics, with persistent issues in mobile competition, regulatory delays, incomplete strategic alliances, and high costs affecting business competitiveness.
